newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Mandela requests Chiluba to postpone Zambian poll.
newsitem.headline: Mandela requests Chiluba to postpone Zambian poll.

text.p: South African President Nelson Mandela said on Thursday he had asked Zambian leader Frederick Chiluba to postpone the country's elections due next week.

"This morning I sent an urgent fax (recommending to Chiluba) that he must...postpone the elections in the interests of peace in the country," Mandela told a news conference in the port city of Durban.

Mandela said Chiluba had two options, either postpone the elections or declare a state of emergency in the southern African country which would result in an automatic postponement of the poll due on November 18.

"President Chiluba can take one of two options to do this. One is to declare a state of emergency which would automatically postpone the elections and the second, it is his prerogative in terms of the law to postpone the elections."

Seven opposition parties, including former president Kenneth Kaunda's United National Independence Party (UNIP), are boycotting the elections which they say have been arranged to ensure that Chiluba's Movement for Multi-party Democracy (MMD) remains in office.
The parties oppose a new constitution barring some candidates, including Kaunda, from standing for president if they are first-generation Zambians.
